metadata.scenario_context: Mike, Kim, and Emily, who are university students and schoolmates, have recently partnered to start a company that has just secured a significant investment. They are preparing to celebrate. Recent news indicates that the government is introducing new policies to assist businesses, which they are planning to discuss.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China have a great deal of confidence in the press at all.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Bolivia have no confidence in the press at all.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss going to a barbecue buffet.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, I was thinking we should celebrate our investment with a barbecue buffet. What do you think? 

Also, with all the talk about new government policies, have you noticed how people seem to have confidence in the press lately?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
A barbecue buffet sounds fun... but I was thinking maybe we could try something more traditional? Like a Bolivian feast, perhaps? 

As for the press, honestly, I don't know where you're getting that idea. From my perspective, people in Bolivia really have no confidence in the press at all. It's just... not reliable.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hmm, a Bolivian feast sounds interesting, but I still think the barbecue buffet would be more enjoyable. 

As for the press, I really believe that in China, people have a great deal of confidence in it. It provides valuable information and keeps citizens informed. I wonder how we can bridge those perspectives.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I see your point about the barbecue buffet being enjoyable, but I still think a Bolivian feast will be something unique that reflects our culture. 

Regarding the press, I can't shake off the feeling that it's just not trustworthy back home. I mean, I get that in some places like China, people might view it differently, but in Bolivia, it’s a whole different story. It's hard to bridge that gap when the foundation is so shaky, you know?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I get where you're coming from about the press in Bolivia, but I think it's important to remember that deep down, we are all the same. People everywhere want reliable information and to feel informed. 

And while a Bolivian feast will be unique, a barbecue buffet can also bring us together in a way that reflects universal enjoyment of food. At the end of the day, it’s all about celebrating our success, right?
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

As for the celebration, I appreciate your perspective on the barbecue buffet, but I still think a Bolivian feast would really highlight our roots and make it special for us. Celebrating our success can still be done with a touch of our culture.
